prompt: What is an amine?

choices.text: An organic derivative of ammonia, NH3, in which one or more H atoms are replaced by organic groups
Any compound containing oxygen and nitrogen
choices.why: An amine is specifically ammonia with H atoms replaced by organic (R) groups.

choices.text: The combination of an amine group and a carbonyl group
choices.why: That's an amide.

choices.text: An alcohol in which S replaces O
choices.why: That's a thiol.

explanation: An amine is an organic derivative of ammonia (NH3), in which one or more of the H atoms is substituted with an organic group.

prompt: What is a primary amine?

choices.text: An amine in which one H atom of NH3 is replaced by an R group
An amine in which two H atoms are replaced by R groups
choices.why: That's a secondary amine.

choices.text: An amine in which all three H atoms are replaced by R groups
choices.why: That's a tertiary amine.

choices.text: The most important amine in a molecule
choices.why: Primary refers to how many H atoms of NH3 are replaced: one.

explanation: A primary amine has one H atom of NH3 substituted with an R group, a secondary amine two, and a tertiary amine all three.

prompt: Which statement describes a secondary amine?

choices.text: Two of the H atoms of NH3 are replaced by R groups, leaving one H on the N.
Only one H atom is replaced by an R group.
choices.why: That's a primary amine.

choices.text: All three H atoms are replaced.
choices.why: That's a tertiary amine.

choices.text: The N atom is bonded to a carbonyl group.
choices.why: That's an amide.

explanation: A secondary amine has two H atoms substituted with R groups, so one H remains on the nitrogen.

prompt: A tertiary amine has how many H atoms left on its nitrogen?

choices.text: None; all three H atoms of NH3 are replaced by R groups.
One
choices.why: One H left on N means two were replaced: a secondary amine.

choices.text: Two
choices.why: Two H left means only one was replaced: a primary amine.

choices.text: Three
choices.why: Three H atoms on N with no R group is ammonia itself.

explanation: A tertiary amine has all three H atoms of NH3 substituted with R groups.

prompt: Is (CH3CH2)2NH a primary, secondary, or tertiary amine?

choices.text: Secondary
Primary
choices.why: Two ethyl groups replace two H atoms; a primary amine has only one R group.

choices.text: Tertiary
choices.why: One H still remains on the N, so only two H atoms are replaced.

choices.text: It isn't an amine.
choices.why: It is ammonia with two H atoms replaced by ethyl groups: an amine.

explanation: The N carries two ethyl groups and one H, so two of ammonia's H atoms are replaced: a secondary amine.

prompt: Is CH3CH2CH2NH2 a primary, secondary, or tertiary amine?

choices.text: Primary
Secondary
choices.why: Only one R group (propyl) is on the N; two H atoms remain.

choices.text: Tertiary
choices.why: A tertiary amine has no H on the N; this one has two.

choices.text: It is an amide.
choices.why: There's no carbonyl group, so it's an amine, not an amide.

explanation: One H of NH3 is replaced by a propyl group, leaving NH2: a primary amine, propylamine.

prompt: Is (CH3)2NCH2CH3 a primary, secondary, or tertiary amine?

choices.text: Tertiary
Secondary
choices.why: Count the R groups on N: two methyls and an ethyl make three, with no H left.

choices.text: Primary
choices.why: A primary amine has one R group; this N has three.

choices.text: It isn't an amine, because it has no NH2.
choices.why: Tertiary amines have no H on N; they are still amines.

explanation: The N is bonded to two methyl groups and an ethyl group, so all three H atoms of NH3 are replaced: a tertiary amine.

prompt: A nitrogen atom is bonded to one ethyl group and two methyl groups. What is the amine's name?

choices.text: Ethyldimethylamine
Dimethylethylamine
choices.why: Substituents are listed alphabetically, ignoring prefixes like di-: ethyl before methyl.

choices.text: Ethylmethylamine
choices.why: There are two methyl groups, so the prefix di- is needed.

choices.text: Trimethylamine
choices.why: One of the three groups is ethyl, not methyl.

explanation: Name the R groups as substituents, in alphabetical order with numerical prefixes as needed, and add -amine: ethyldimethylamine.

prompt: What is the name of CH3CH2CH2NH2?

choices.text: Propylamine
Propanamide
choices.why: An amide would need a carbonyl group. This is an amine with a propyl group.

choices.text: Propanol
choices.why: -ol is for alcohols. This compound has an NH2 group.

choices.text: Dipropylamine
choices.why: Only one propyl group is on the N.

explanation: Name the R group as a substituent and add the suffix -amine: one propyl group gives propylamine.

prompt: A nitrogen atom is bonded to three propyl groups. What is the amine's name?

choices.text: Tripropylamine
Propylamine
choices.why: There are three propyl groups, so the prefix tri- is needed.

choices.text: Tripropylamide
choices.why: There's no carbonyl group; it is an amine.

choices.text: Nonylamine
choices.why: The three propyl groups are separate substituents on N, not one nine-carbon chain.

explanation: Three identical R groups take the prefix tri-: tripropylamine, a tertiary amine.

prompt: How do amines behave as acids or bases?

choices.text: They are weak bases: the N atom accepts a proton onto its lone electron pair.
They are strong bases, like NaOH.
choices.why: All amines are weak bases, about as weak as carboxylic acids are as acids.

choices.text: They are weak acids that donate H^+.
choices.why: Like NH3, amines accept protons, so they are bases.

choices.text: They are neither acids nor bases.
choices.why: The N's lone pair accepts a proton, making amines Brønsted-Lowry bases.

explanation: As with NH3, the N atom in amines can accept a proton onto its lone electron pair, so amines are Brønsted-Lowry bases. All amines are weak bases.

prompt: What forms when ethylamine, CH3CH2NH2, reacts with HCl?

choices.text: The ion CH3CH2NH3^+ (with Cl^−), the organic counterpart of the ammonium ion
CH3CH2Cl and NH3
choices.why: The amine accepts a proton onto N; the C–N bond stays intact.

choices.text: An amide and water
choices.why: An amide forms with a carboxylic acid, not HCl.

choices.text: No reaction, because amines are weak
choices.why: Weak bases still react with strong acids like HCl, accepting a proton.

explanation: The amine accepts a proton and becomes an ion, CH3CH2NH3^+, the organic counterpart of the ammonium (NH4^+) ion.

prompt: According to the section, how weak are amines as bases?

choices.text: About as weak as carboxylic acids are as acids
As strong as NaOH
choices.why: All amines are weak bases.

choices.text: So weak that they don't accept protons at all
choices.why: Amines do accept protons; they are weak but real bases.

choices.text: Stronger than any inorganic base
choices.why: Amines are weak bases, comparable in weakness to carboxylic acids.

explanation: All amines are weak bases; the weakness of amines is about the same as that of carboxylic acids. N-containing organic compounds in nature also act as weak bases.

prompt: What is an amide functional group?

choices.text: A combination of an amine group and a carbonyl group
An amine with three R groups
choices.why: That's a tertiary amine. An amide has its N bonded to a carbonyl carbon.

choices.text: An alcohol in which N replaces O
choices.why: An amide combines an amine group with a carbonyl group.

choices.text: A carbonyl bonded to an O–R group
choices.why: That's an ester.

explanation: An amide functional group is a combination of an amine group and a carbonyl group.

prompt: How is an amide formed?

choices.text: An amine and a carboxylic acid combine, losing a molecule of H2O.
An amine and an alcohol combine, losing H2.
choices.why: Amides form from an amine and a carboxylic acid, with water lost.

choices.text: An amine reacts with HCl.
choices.why: That gives an ammonium-type ion, not an amide.

choices.text: A carboxylic acid loses CO2.
choices.why: The amine's N bonds to the acid's carbonyl C as water is lost.

explanation: Amides are formed by bringing together an amine and a carboxylic acid; a molecule of H2O is lost, much like when an ester forms.

prompt: What is an amide bond?

choices.text: The bond between the N of the amine group and the C of the carbonyl group
The bond between N and H in an amine
choices.why: The amide bond links the amine's N to the carbonyl C.

choices.text: A bond between two S atoms
choices.why: That's a disulfide bond, between cysteine units.

choices.text: A hydrogen bond between two amines
choices.why: An amide bond is a covalent N–C bond to a carbonyl carbon.

explanation: The bond between the N of the amine group and the C of the carbonyl group is called an amide bond. Amide bonds hold proteins together.

prompt: What is an amino acid?

choices.text: A molecule that has both an amine group and a carboxylic acid group
Any acid that contains nitrogen, like HNO3
choices.why: Amino acids are organic molecules with an amine group and a carboxylic acid group.

choices.text: A thiol
choices.why: Some amino acids, like cysteine, contain a thiol, but all have amine and carboxylic acid groups.

choices.text: A protein
choices.why: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, which are long chains of them.

explanation: Amino acids are molecules that have an amine group and a carboxylic acid group. The amine of one reacts with the acid of another, so proteins are chains of amino acids held together by amide bonds.

prompt: Four amino acids are joined in a straight chain by amide bonds. How many amide bonds hold the chain together?
explanation: Each amide bond joins two neighboring amino acids, so a chain of 4 has 4 − 1 = 3 amide bonds.

prompt: Five amino acids are joined into a straight chain. How many molecules of H2O are released?
explanation: Each amide bond releases one H2O, and a chain of 5 amino acids has 4 amide bonds, so 4 H2O are released.

prompt: What is a thiol?

choices.text: The sulfur analog of an alcohol, R–SH
An organic derivative of ammonia
choices.why: That's an amine.

choices.text: A compound with an S–S bond
choices.why: An S–S bond is a disulfide bond, formed when two thiols are oxidized.

choices.text: An ether with sulfur
choices.why: A thiol has an SH group, like an alcohol's OH.

explanation: Sulfur is below oxygen in the periodic table, and an S atom can take the place of the O in an alcohol, giving R–SH: a thiol.

prompt: A five-carbon chain has an SH group on its first carbon. What is its formal name?

choices.text: 1-pentanethiol
1-pentanol
choices.why: -ol is for an OH group. With SH, the suffix is -thiol.

choices.text: Pentyl sulfide
choices.why: Thiols are named like alcohols but with the suffix -thiol.

choices.text: 5-pentanethiol
choices.why: Number to give the SH group the lowest number: 1.

explanation: Thiols are named like alcohols, except the suffix is -thiol instead of -ol: 1-pentanethiol.

prompt: In the older system, what is CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2SH called?

choices.text: Pentyl mercaptan
Pentyl alcohol
choices.why: Alcohols have OH. For simple thiols, the older system uses the word mercaptan.

choices.text: Pentanethiol mercaptan
choices.why: Use one system or the other: pentanethiol, or pentyl mercaptan.

choices.text: Butyl mercaptan
choices.why: The chain has five carbons: pentyl.

explanation: An older system names simple thiols with the word mercaptan, much as the word alcohol is used with small alcohols: pentyl mercaptan.

prompt: Why are small amounts of thiols added to natural gas?

choices.text: Natural gas is odorless, and thiols have strong odors, so gas leaks can be detected.
Thiols make the gas burn hotter.
choices.why: They're added only at very low levels, for their smell.

choices.text: Thiols prevent the gas from exploding.
choices.why: Thiols give the odorless gas a smell, so leaks are noticed.

choices.text: Thiols remove water from the gas.
choices.why: Their purpose is their strong odor; skunk spray is made of thiols.

explanation: Many thiols have strong, objectionable odors (skunk spray is made of thiols, detectable below 10 ppb). Because natural gas is odorless, thiols are added at very low levels so leaks can be detected.

prompt: What happens when two cysteine units in a protein chain approach each other and are oxidized?

choices.text: An S–S (disulfide) bond forms: R–SH + HS–R → R–S–S–R.
An amide bond forms between them.
choices.why: Amide bonds link the amino acids in the chain; oxidizing two SH groups forms an S–S bond.

choices.text: They break apart into sulfur atoms.
choices.why: The two SH groups join, forming a disulfide bond.

choices.text: They form an alcohol.
choices.why: Oxidation joins the two sulfurs: R–S–S–R.

explanation: Two cysteine units can be oxidized to form an S–S bond, a disulfide bond, strong enough to fix their positions and impose a structure on the protein.

prompt: What is the primary chemical mechanism behind straightening and curling hair ("perms")?

choices.text: Breaking and remaking disulfide bonds between cysteine units
Breaking the amide bonds of hair proteins
choices.why: Breaking the protein chain itself would destroy the hair. Perms work on the S–S bonds.

choices.text: Adding water to hair
choices.why: The section names the breaking and remaking of disulfide bonds.

choices.text: Turning amines into amides
choices.why: The mechanism involves the disulfide bonds of cysteine, which makes up about 5% of hair.

explanation: Hair is about 5% cysteine, and the breaking and remaking of disulfide bonds between cysteine units is the primary mechanism behind straightening and curling hair.

prompt: What are essential amino acids?

choices.text: Amino acids the body can't make, so they must be obtained from the diet
All of the amino acids in the body
choices.why: The body can make many amino acids itself; only some must come from food.

choices.text: Amino acids that are strong acids
choices.why: Essential refers to the diet: these amino acids can't be made by the body.

choices.text: Amino acids that contain sulfur
choices.why: Essential means the body can't synthesize them, whatever their structure.

explanation: The body can synthesize some amino acids, but others must be obtained from the diet; those are the essential amino acids. That's why a diet balanced in protein matters.

prompt: Why is rice and beans nutritionally notable?

choices.text: Together they provide all of the essential amino acids in one dish.
Rice alone provides all the essential amino acids.
choices.why: Without one of the two components, the dish would be nutritionally incomplete.

choices.text: They contain no protein.
choices.why: Beans are a good protein source; together with rice, they supply all the essential amino acids.

choices.text: They replace the need for any amino acids.
choices.why: The body still needs amino acids; this dish supplies all the essential ones.

explanation: Rice and beans provides all of the essential amino acids in one dish; without one component, it would be nutritionally incomplete. Over-reliance on corn, by contrast, deprives people of lysine and tryptophan.
